name: retry
description: Retries with exponential backoff and jitter, retry budgets, a circuit breaker and rate limiters, on a clock effect that tests run virtually

api.name: clock
api.sig:
pub effect clock
  retry_sleep(ms: Int)
  retry_now() -> Int
api.doc:
The clock the runners use. `retry_sleep(ms)` waits, `retry_now()` is the time in
milliseconds. The `_now` runners handle it with the real clock and `simulate` with a virtual
one; a handler of your own can do anything else (see the README).

api.name: Jitter
api.sig: pub type Jitter = NoJitter | FullJitter | EqualJitter | DecorrelatedJitter derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
How the delay before each retry is randomized (see the AWS Architecture Blog's
"Exponential Backoff And Jitter"): none, uniform in [0, d] (full), d/2 plus uniform in
[0, d/2] (equal), or uniform in [base, 3 * previous delay] (decorrelated).

api.name: Policy
api.sig: pub type Policy = {max_attempts: Int where _ >= 1, base_ms: Int where _ >= 0, multiplier: F64 where _ >= 1.0, max_delay_ms: Int where _ >= 0, jitter: Jitter, budget_ms: Opt[Int], seed: Opt[Int]} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
A retry policy. Attempt `n` (from 1) is followed, when it fails and may be retried, by a
delay of `base_ms * multiplier ** (n - 1)` capped at `max_delay_ms`, then jittered.
`budget_ms` bounds the total time from the first attempt: a retry whose delay would end past
it is not made. `seed` seeds the jitter; `none` takes the clock's time at the start.

api.name: Stop
api.sig: pub type Stop = Succeeded | Exhausted | NotRetryable | BudgetExceeded derive Eq, Show
api.doc: Why a run stopped.

api.name: Outcome
api.sig: pub type Outcome[T, E] = {result: Res[T, E], attempts: Int, delays: List[Int], waited_ms: Int, stop: Stop} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
The result of a run: the last result, the number of attempts made, each delay slept, their
sum, and why it stopped.

api.name: default_policy
api.sig: fn default_policy() -> Policy
api.doc: The default policy: 3 attempts, 100 ms doubling up to 10 s, full jitter, no budget.

api.name: constant
api.sig: fn constant(delay_ms: Int where _ >= 0, attempts: Int where _ >= 1) -> Policy
api.doc: `attempts` attempts with the same `delay_ms` between them and no jitter.

api.name: exponential
api.sig: fn exponential(base_ms: Int where _ >= 0, attempts: Int where _ >= 1) -> Policy
api.doc: `attempts` attempts with delays doubling from `base_ms` up to 30 s, without jitter.

api.name: no_retry
api.sig: fn no_retry() -> Policy
api.doc: One attempt and no retries.

api.name: base_delay
api.sig: fn base_delay(p: Policy, attempt: Int where _ >= 1) -> Int
api.doc:
The delay after failed attempt `attempt` before jitter: `base_ms * multiplier ** (attempt - 1)`
capped at `max_delay_ms` (never overflowing).

api.name: next_delay
api.sig: fn next_delay(p: Policy, attempt: Int where _ >= 1, prev_ms: Int, seed: Int) -> (Int, Int)
api.doc:
The jittered delay after failed attempt `attempt`, given the previous delay (`base_ms` before
the first retry; only decorrelated jitter uses it) and a seed. Gives the delay and the next
seed; the same inputs always give the same delay, which is never above `max_delay_ms`.

api.name: schedule
api.sig: fn schedule(p: Policy) -> List[Int]
api.doc:
The delays a run sleeps when every attempt fails: one per retry, `max_attempts - 1` in all,
from `seed` (or 0 when the policy has none). Ignores the budget.

api.name: worst_case_ms
api.sig: fn worst_case_ms(p: Policy) -> Int
api.doc:
The longest total time a run can sleep: the sum of the delays before jitter (decorrelated
jitter can reach `max_delay_ms` on every retry, so it counts that).

api.name: run_hinted
api.sig: fn run_hinted[T, E, e](p: Policy, op: Int -> Res[T, E] ! e, retryable: E -> Bool, after: E -> Opt[Int]) -> Outcome[T, E] ! clock, e
api.doc:
Runs `op(attempt)` (attempts count from 1) until it succeeds, `retryable` says an error is
final, the attempts run out or the budget would be exceeded. `after(e)` may give a delay the
error asks for, such as an HTTP Retry-After, which replaces the computed one (negative values
count as 0); it is still bounded by the budget.

api.name: run_when
api.sig: fn run_when[T, E, e](p: Policy, op: Int -> Res[T, E] ! e, retryable: E -> Bool) -> Outcome[T, E] ! clock, e
api.doc: `run_hinted` without delay hints.

api.name: run
api.sig: fn run[T, E, e](p: Policy, op: Int -> Res[T, E] ! e) -> Outcome[T, E] ! clock, e
api.doc: `run_hinted` retrying every error, without delay hints.

api.name: run_hinted_now
api.sig: fn run_hinted_now[T, E, e](p: Policy, op: Int -> Res[T, E] ! e, retryable: E -> Bool, after: E -> Opt[Int]) -> Outcome[T, E] ! time, e
api.doc: `run_hinted` on the real clock: it sleeps with `sleep_ms` and reads `now_ms`.

api.name: run_now
api.sig: fn run_now[T, E, e](p: Policy, op: Int -> Res[T, E] ! e) -> Outcome[T, E] ! time, e
api.doc: `run` on the real clock.

api.name: simulate_hinted
api.sig: fn simulate_hinted[T, E, e](start_ms: Int, p: Policy, op: Int -> Res[T, E] ! e, retryable: E -> Bool, after: E -> Opt[Int]) -> (Outcome[T, E], Int) ! e
api.doc:
`run_hinted` on a virtual clock that starts at `start_ms` and moves only when the runner
sleeps, so nothing really waits. Gives the outcome and the virtual time at the end.

api.name: simulate
api.sig: fn simulate[T, E, e](start_ms: Int, p: Policy, op: Int -> Res[T, E] ! e) -> (Outcome[T, E], Int) ! e
api.doc: `run` on a virtual clock that starts at `start_ms` (see `simulate_hinted`).

api.name: BreakerConfig
api.sig: pub type BreakerConfig = {failure_threshold: Int where _ >= 1, failure_rate: F64 where _ > 0.0 and _ <= 1.0, min_calls: Int where _ >= 1, window_ms: Int where _ >= 1, cooldown_ms: Int where _ >= 0, half_open_trials: Int where _ >= 1} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
When a breaker trips and how it recovers. It opens when, among the calls of the last
`window_ms`, there are `failure_threshold` failures, or at least `min_calls` calls of which
a `failure_rate` share or more failed. It stays open for `cooldown_ms`, then lets
`half_open_trials` calls through: all of them succeeding closes it, any failure opens it again.

api.name: BreakerState
api.sig: pub type BreakerState = Closed | Open{until_ms: Int} | HalfOpen{started: Int, succeeded: Int} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
A breaker's state: closed (calls go through), open until a time, or half open with the number
of trial calls let through and the number that succeeded.

api.name: Breaker
api.sig: pub type Breaker = {config: BreakerConfig, state: BreakerState, events: List[(Int, Bool)]} derive Eq, Show
api.doc: A circuit breaker: its configuration, its state and the recent calls `(time_ms, succeeded)`.

api.name: Called
api.sig: pub type Called[T, E] = Rejected{wait_ms: Int} | Ran{result: Res[T, E]} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
What `call` did: refused the call (the breaker is open; a call may go through in `wait_ms`),
or ran it with this result.

api.name: default_breaker_config
api.sig: fn default_breaker_config() -> BreakerConfig
api.doc:
The default breaker configuration: 5 failures, or half of at least 20 calls, within 60 s;
open for 30 s; one trial call.

api.name: breaker
api.sig: fn breaker(config: BreakerConfig) -> Breaker
api.doc: A closed breaker with no history.

api.name: window_counts
api.sig: fn window_counts(b: Breaker, now: Int) -> (Int, Int)
api.doc: The calls and failures the breaker counts at `now`, those of the last `window_ms`.

api.name: current_state
api.sig: fn current_state(b: Breaker, now: Int) -> BreakerState
api.doc: The state at `now`: an open breaker whose cool-down has passed reads as half open.

api.name: ms_until_allowed
api.sig: fn ms_until_allowed(b: Breaker, now: Int) -> Int
api.doc:
How long until a call may go through: 0 when it may now. While every half-open trial is in
flight their results decide, and it gives `cooldown_ms`, the wait if one of them fails.

api.name: allow
api.sig: fn allow(b: Breaker, now: Int) -> (Bool, Breaker)
api.doc:
Asks to make a call at `now`: whether it may go through, and the breaker after counting it
(an open breaker past its cool-down becomes half open and starts a trial).

api.name: record_success
api.sig: fn record_success(b: Breaker, now: Int) -> Breaker
api.doc:
Records a successful call at `now`. In the half-open state the last needed trial success
closes the breaker and clears its history.

api.name: record_failure
api.sig: fn record_failure(b: Breaker, now: Int) -> Breaker
api.doc:
Records a failed call at `now`: a closed breaker opens when the failures reach the limits, a
half-open one opens again at once.

api.name: call_when
api.sig: fn call_when[T, E, e](b: Breaker, now: Int, op: () -> Res[T, E] ! e, counts: E -> Bool) -> (Called[T, E], Breaker) ! e
api.doc:
Runs `op` through the breaker at `now`, counting the errors for which `counts(e)` holds as
failures and every other result as a success (so a "not found" need not trip it).

api.name: call
api.sig: fn call[T, E, e](b: Breaker, now: Int, op: () -> Res[T, E] ! e) -> (Called[T, E], Breaker) ! e
api.doc: `call_when` counting every error as a failure.

api.name: Bucket
api.sig: pub type Bucket = {capacity: Int where _ >= 1, per_sec: F64 where _ > 0.0, tokens: F64, updated_ms: Int} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
A token bucket: up to `capacity` tokens, refilled continuously at `per_sec` tokens a second;
`tokens` were left at `updated_ms`.

api.name: Window
api.sig: pub type Window = {limit: Int where _ >= 1, window_ms: Int where _ >= 1, hits: List[Int]} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
A sliding window limiter: at most `limit` calls in any `window_ms`; `hits` are the times of the
calls still in the window.

api.name: bucket
api.sig: fn bucket(capacity: Int where _ >= 1, per_sec: F64 where _ > 0.0, now: Int) -> Bucket
api.doc: A full bucket of `capacity` tokens at `now`.

api.name: bucket_tokens
api.sig: fn bucket_tokens(b: Bucket, now: Int) -> F64
api.doc: The tokens available at `now` (a time before `updated_ms` refills nothing).

api.name: bucket_take
api.sig: fn bucket_take(b: Bucket, now: Int, n: Int where _ >= 0) -> (Bool, Bucket)
api.doc: Takes `n` tokens at `now` if they are there: whether it did, and the bucket after.

api.name: bucket_wait_ms
api.sig: fn bucket_wait_ms(b: Bucket, now: Int, n: Int where _ >= 0) -> Opt[Int]
api.doc:
How long until `n` tokens are there: 0 when they are now, `none` when `n` is more than the
capacity (they never will be).

api.name: window_limiter
api.sig: fn window_limiter(limit: Int where _ >= 1, window_ms: Int where _ >= 1) -> Window
api.doc: An empty sliding window limiter.

api.name: window_remaining
api.sig: fn window_remaining(w: Window, now: Int) -> Int
api.doc: How many more calls the window allows at `now`.

api.name: window_take
api.sig: fn window_take(w: Window, now: Int) -> (Bool, Window)
api.doc: Counts a call at `now` if the window allows it: whether it did, and the limiter after.

api.name: window_wait_ms
api.sig: fn window_wait_ms(w: Window, now: Int) -> Int
api.doc: How long until the window allows a call: 0 when it does now.
